target_customer: Established multi-location home service companies (HVAC, plumbing, roofing, solar, smart home) and PE backed portfolios
problem: Home service companies struggle to get found and recommended on Google, Maps and AI search, and to collect reviews from frontline employees.
business_model: Done-for-you local visibility service (managed fee); launched as an NFC review capture product for in-person employees
product_category: Local SEO and generative engine optimization for service businesses

founders.name: Dylan Allen-Arnegard
founders.background_notes: YC page lists more than 5 years of frontline roles; the launch post describes the Podium and Weave work less as internships.

founders.name: Amadeus Peterson
prior_employers: Northrop Grumman (Sentinel Missile system software engineer)

technical_complexity.rationale: The original NFC review capture app and the current managed local SEO and AI visibility tracking are mostly standard software and services work.

defensibility.rationale: Review and local SEO services are offered by many vendors and agencies, and a done-for-you service has little technical lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established review and local marketing platforms already served home services; no acquisition of Cheers found.

market_need_then: Home service firms rely on Google reviews and local search for leads, and by 2025 AI search recommendations created a new visibility problem.

identity.visual_style: Clean modern site with a topographic background motif

brand_strength.rationale: Very generic name shared with many unrelated companies (a social app, a drink brand, others), and search found no press about the brand itself.

pivots.from: Super-app for in-person employees with NFC review badges
pivots.to: Cheers GEO, a platform to win local search on AI assistants, later a done-for-you local visibility service
pivots.why: Not stated; Product Hunt launches show Aug 2024 and Oct 2025 positioning.

outcome_analysis: Cheers launched in S24 as a review capture app for frontline workers and moved to AI search visibility for home service companies, claiming 70,000 reviews collected for Vivint in five months, which is self-reported. Funding is unverified, the team is small and the category is crowded, so the traction story is unclear. No shutdown or acquisition was found.
notes: Standout.work lists a Series A of $2.5M and startups.fm lists $500K total raised; no primary announcement or second outlet confirmed either, so unverified and no round recorded. Team size shows 6 in the queue file and 2 or 5 in other listings. The competitor search returned only 2025 and 2026 comparison pages for Podium, Birdeye, Housecall Pro and NiceJob, none dated near mid 2024, so the list is empty. Many unrelated companies named Cheers were ignored.
